title: CS25 Fourier pair-identity = the LineIncidence spectral identity = the Gauss-period sup-norm M(n), via the SAME dual-code Parseval — cross-cone identification of F2/F3/F16/F18
connection: CS25 fourier_pair_identity: |G|·#{(w,f)∈B²:w−f∈C}=∑_{ψ:Ĝ}Ŝ(ψ)Ŝ(−ψ), G=Fⁿ/C, Ŝ(ψ)=∑_{w∈B}ψ(⟦w⟧). ψ=0 term is |B|²; off-diagonal q^{k−n}∑_{ψ≠0}‖Ŝ(ψ)‖² is a DUAL-CODE character sum. This equals LineIncidenceSpectral.lineIncidence_spectral: #{γ:s₀+γs₁∈S}·|V|=|F|·∑_{ψ⊥s₁}∑_{s∈S}ψ(s₀−s) (only s₁^⊥ survives the γ-average). Choosing B=syndrome ball, C^⊥ generated by the line direction, the surviving dual frequencies' worst Fourier coefficient is EXACTLY M(n)=max_b|∑_{x∈μ_n}e_p(bx)| (F2). So CS25's second-moment Parseval and the prize's incomplete-character-sum sup-norm are the SAME Parseval mass, B²-pair-counted (CS25, L²) vs worst-frequency (prize, L^∞).
why_insightful: CS25's identity is universally read as averaging; recognizing it is the W4/Gauss-period Parseval (identical to LineIncidenceSpectral) shows CS25 already contains the prize's spectral object — and explains WHY CS25 only reaches Johnson: it bounds L² mass (free) but the prize needs the single worst ‖Ŝ(ψ)‖, which CS25 discards.
attack_plan: Lean: cs25_fourier_offdiag_eq_lineIncidence_spectralError instantiating fourier_pair_identity with C=ker of line-evaluation and B=syndrome ball, rewrite via lineIncidence_spectral to expose ∑_{ψ⊥s₁}‖Ŝ(ψ)‖². Probe (μ_8/μ_16, p=12289): compute both sides, confirm the worst dual frequency = measured M(n); lets any future M(n)≤C√(n log(p/n)) feed CS25's E[N²] through a proven bridge.
